answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can employ a Sybil resistance mechanism known as "reputation mirroring". Each agent maintains a reputation score, which is echoed throughout the network, reflecting its honest participation. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities will find it costly to maintain a consistent, high reputation across all Sybil nodes, as their fake identities will not mirror the expected behavior, akin to the fable of the boy who cried wolf, where the community becomes skeptical of repeated claims.
